secondarySuiteDefinition.text: A secondary suite is a self-contained dwelling unit in a building of only residential occupancy that contains only one other dwelling unit and common spaces, where both units form a single real estate entity (one title).
secondarySuiteDefinition.implication: The Code's 'house with a secondary suite' provisions used in this pack apply only when the house has exactly two dwelling units. routes.summary: Create an additional dwelling unit (ADU; Kitchener's term for an ARU, and a 'duplex' when the house has two units): a separate home with its own kitchen, bathroom and entrance. It must meet zoning (By-law 2019-051 s. 4.12 or By-law 85-1 s. 5.22), get a building permit, meet the Code's 'house with a secondary suite' rules (fire separation, interconnected alarms, exits, HVAC) and get an ESA permit. A zoning (occupancy) certificate is not needed for a duplex. No general rental licence was found in Kitchener. Ontario's Planning Act s. 35.1 stops zoning from banning up to 3 units on a serviced residential lot; Kitchener allows up to 4. Province-wide limits also stop zoning from requiring more than 1 parking space per ARU, setting a minimum unit size, or requiring the owner to live there.
routes.permit: City of Kitchener building permit for a duplex (adding one ADU): $0.37 per sq ft of finished space (minimum $163 per the permits page; the 2026 fee schedule lists only a general $95 minimum), plus a $250 rebate fee refunded when the final inspection passes. The City says it reviews a complete application within 10 business days; the Building Code's legal maximum for a house with one unit above another is 15 days (Div. C Table 1.3.1.3 Item 2).

rules.notes: Kitchener has two zoning by-laws in force: 2019-051 (about 80% of lots) and 85-1 (about 20%); check which one applies in the City's property zoning viewer (https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/c870484f904744b8bb4f1bdecf18dddb). Both allow 4 units after the 'Enabling Four Units' amendments (By-laws 2024-074 and 2024-073, effective 2024-03-25). The 2019-051 section PDFs carry no printed consolidation date; dates are from the PDF files and the latest amendment each cites. Two or three attached ADUs (s. 4.12.2) add rules a single basement unit does not have: minimum lot width 10.5 m outside the LRT/Central Neighbourhood areas, street-facing door limits, and 20% front / 30% rear landscaping. ADUs are not allowed in the EUF-1 floodplain zone (see zoning_floodplain_regulated_area). The Building Code's 'house with a secondary suite' rules only apply when the house has exactly 2 units (see codeInForce.secondarySuiteDefinition).

rules.title: A safe way out of the suite
rules.plain: Best: the suite has its own door to the outside. A shared exit is allowed if it is separated by a 30-minute fire separation, does not pass through the other home or a service room, and both homes have interconnected smoke alarms. Leaving through the other home is only allowed with an extra escape window and interconnected alarms, or if the house is sprinklered.

options: (a) own_exterior_door: a door (including a sliding door) that opens directly to the exterior from the dwelling unit, serves only that unit, has reasonable access to ground level, and the units have smoke alarms per 9.10.19

(c) through_other_unit_plus_escape_window: access to exit leads through the other unit and an extra escape window is provided: sill not more than 1,000 mm above or below adjacent ground, openable without tools, opening at least 0.38 m2 with no dimension under 460 mm, sill not more than 900 mm above the floor or fixed steps, and at least 1,000 mm clear in a window well; interconnected smoke alarms in every unit and common area

(d) sprinklered: the building is sprinklered and the units have smoke alarms per 9.10.19
